answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on a task, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. If votes are weighted by stake and newly created accounts gain no extra influence, splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply voting power; each account must lock real value. A raven-like audit network can sample claims, while yarrow and zenith mark separate audit rounds, forcing an attacker to risk capital repeatedly rather than minting costless identities.
